lines: Eight VCAs in two groups of four, each group also summed to a mix output at the centre of its black hole

Sets the level of that channel, silent at the centre, full clockwise and full with the phase inverted anticlockwise; with no cable in that channel's input it sends a fixed voltage instead, 10V at full
Switches the four level knobs of that black hole from a linear response to an exponential one
Feeds the top black hole's mix into every channel of the bottom group whose input is empty, turning that group into four separate treatments of the top mix
Sets the voltage the level CV inputs of that black hole need for a full sweep, plus or minus 5V or plus or minus 10V, shown by the lit 5V or 10V lamp
The signal into that channel, which is multiplied by the channel's level and sent both to its own output and to the black hole mix
Adds to the level knob of that channel, a full sweep taking 5V or 10V according to the gravity setting of that black hole
That channel's input at the level set for it, or a fixed voltage from the level knob alone when the channel input is empty
The four channels of that black hole added together, clamped to plus or minus 10V
Two rotating crossfaders: the top one blends eight inputs down to one output, the bottom one spreads one input across eight outputs
One of the eight signals the top pulsar rotates through, crossfaded with the next one as the rotation passes between them
The top pulsar's crossfade between the input it has reached and the next one in the rotation
The signal the bottom pulsar spreads across its outputs; with nothing patched here each output takes the top pulsar's input jack at the matching point of the circle
Carries the bottom pulsar's input while the rotation has reached this jack, fading in and out as the rotation passes it
Drives the rotation of the top pulsar, the voltage read across the range set by that pulsar's polarity button
Drives the rotation of the bottom pulsar, and with nothing patched here the bottom pulsar follows the voltage at the top pulsar's rotation input
Includes the empty jacks of that pulsar in the rotation, so the rotation passes through silence where no cable is patched; with it off only the patched jacks are visited
A trigger here switches that pulsar between rotating through every jack and rotating through only the patched ones
Turns that pulsar's rotation the other way round the circle
A trigger here reverses the direction of that pulsar's rotation
Makes that pulsar pick its next jack at random instead of the next one round the circle, and shuffles the order of the jacks in the all-jacks reading of the rotation input
Steps that pulsar's rotation input through three readings: minus 5V to 5V, 0V to 10V, and a third where one 0V to 10V sweep runs across all of that pulsar's connected jacks
Note — neither pulsar rotates by itself; each needs a moving voltage at its rotation input, and with nothing patched there it rests on one jack
Fourteen sample and holds in two groups of seven, each with its own noise source, triggered by one input per group
Pink noise between minus 5V and 5V, sampled on each trigger of the top brane; the other pink hold of that brane is inverted while both are used
Red noise between minus 5V and 5V, sampled on each trigger of the top brane; the other red hold of that brane is inverted while both are used
Blue noise between minus 5V and 5V, sampled on each trigger of the top brane; the other blue hold of that brane is inverted while both are used
White noise between minus 5V and 5V, or 0V to 10V with that brane's range switched, sampled on each trigger of the top brane
Blue noise between minus 5V and 5V, or 0V to 10V with that brane's range switched, sampled on each trigger of the top brane; the other blue hold of that brane is inverted while both are used
Red noise between minus 5V and 5V, or 0V to 10V with that brane's range switched, sampled on each trigger of the top brane; the other red hold of that brane is inverted while both are used
Pink noise between minus 5V and 5V, or 0V to 10V with that brane's range switched, sampled by both of the trigger inputs; the other pink hold of that brane is inverted while both are used
Pink noise between minus 5V and 5V, or 0V to 1V with that brane's range switched, sampled on each trigger of the bottom brane; the other pink hold of that brane is inverted while both are used
Red noise between minus 5V and 5V, or 0V to 1V with that brane's range switched, sampled on each trigger of the bottom brane; the other red hold of that brane is inverted while both are used
Blue noise between minus 5V and 5V, or 0V to 1V with that brane's range switched, sampled on each trigger of the bottom brane; the other blue hold of that brane is inverted while both are used
White noise between minus 5V and 5V, or 0V to 1V with that brane's range switched, sampled on each trigger of the bottom brane
Blue noise between minus 5V and 5V, or minus 1V to 1V with that brane's range switched, sampled on each trigger of the bottom brane; the other blue hold of that brane is inverted while both are used
Red noise between minus 5V and 5V, or minus 1V to 1V with that brane's range switched, sampled on each trigger of the bottom brane; the other red hold of that brane is inverted while both are used
Pink noise between minus 5V and 5V, or minus 1V to 1V with that brane's range switched, sampled by both of the trigger inputs; the other pink hold of that brane is inverted while both are used
Feeds the hold beside it: a trigger at that brane captures the voltage here in place of the noise, and with no trigger reaching that hold the voltage here passes through continuously
A rising edge here holds all seven values of the top brane, and the bottom left pink one as well
A rising edge here holds all seven values of the bottom brane, and the top right pink one as well
Turns that brane's trigger off and on; a two second hold reaches the random modes, where presses alternate between triggering one connected output at random and giving each an even chance
A trigger here turns that brane's trigger input off and on
Switches the top brane's white hold and its three right hand holds from noise between minus 5V and 5V to noise between 0V and 10V
Switches the bottom brane's noise away from minus 5V to 5V: its white hold and three right hand holds run 0V to 1V, and its three left hand holds run minus 1V to 1V
A trigger here switches that brane's noise range
Note — no value is held until a trigger arrives at one of the two trigger inputs
Menu — High brane Young mode (long push) — puts the top brane into the random trigger modes, the state a two second hold of its trigger button reaches
Menu — Low brane Young mode (long push) — puts the bottom brane into the random trigger modes, the state a two second hold of its trigger button reaches
Branes.notes: The two 'Young mode' menu items are the same states the panel reaches by holding a brane's trigger button for two seconds; the panel prints no name for them. Each brane generates one value per noise colour and hands the second jack of that colour the inverted copy, so the inversion only appears while both jacks of a pair are patched.

lines: A dual CV sequencer whose fifteen step knobs form two eight-step rings sharing one knob, with either voice able to jump from one ring to the other
Sets the voltage of the first step of both rings, read by whichever voice has reached that step
Sets the voltage of that step of the blue ring, spread over the blue range and quantized while the blue Planck constant is on
Sets the voltage of that step of the yellow ring, spread over the yellow range and quantized while the yellow Planck constant is on
Starts and stops both voices
Returns both voices to the shared first step
Sets the chance of a voice jumping to the other ring when a jump is offered, none fully anticlockwise and certain fully clockwise
Every volt here adds a tenth to the chance of a jump, on top of the probability knob
Offers a jump to the other ring at every step instead of only at the last step of a ring
A trigger here turns the jump at every step on and off
Steps the voltage that voice's step knobs cover: 0-1V, minus 1V to 2V or minus 2V to 3V while its Planck constant is on, and plus or minus 1V, 5V or 10V while it is off
Sets the range of that voice and overrides its button: 1V and above the widest, minus 1V and below the narrowest, and between them the middle one
Steps which clock advances that voice: the global clock, that voice's own local clock, or both of them
Sets which clock advances that voice and overrides its button: 1V and above the global clock, minus 1V and below the local one, and between them both
A rising edge here advances every voice set to take the global clock, unless that voice's local clock fired on the same sample
A rising edge here advances that voice while it is set to take its local clock, by one step, or by a weighted random 1 to 8 steps while uncertainty is on
Makes a pulse at a local clock input advance its voice by a weighted random 1 to 8 steps instead of one
A trigger here turns the random step count on and off
Advances both voices by one step for each press
Returns both voices to the shared first step whenever run is switched on
Quantizes that voice's output to semitones, and narrows the voltage its range covers
A trigger here starts and stops both voices
A rising edge here returns both voices to the shared first step
The voltage of the knob the blue voice has reached, in whichever ring it is travelling
The voltage of the knob the yellow voice has reached, in whichever ring it is travelling
A 1ms 10V pulse each time that voice jumps from one ring to the other
Note — the sequence does not advance until a clock arrives; the module comes up running, and the run button stops and starts it
An eight-step sequencer holding a blue and a yellow value at every step, playing one of the two by chance, or both added together
Sets the blue value of that step: a voltage within the blue range with fixed CV chosen, the span of the blue random draw with random chosen, or the gain on the blue external signal
Sets the yellow value of that step: a voltage within the yellow range with fixed CV chosen, the span of the yellow random draw with random chosen, or the gain on the yellow external signal
Sets the chance that this step plays its blue value rather than its yellow one, always yellow fully anticlockwise and always blue fully clockwise
Shifts the blue chance of every step, clockwise towards yellow and anticlockwise towards blue, across the whole span of the step knobs
Shifts the blue chance of every step at a fifth of that span per volt, positive voltages pushing towards yellow, and adds to the global probability knob
Steps the voltage that colour's step knobs cover: 0-1V, minus 1V to 2V or minus 2V to 3V while its Planck constant is on, and plus or minus 1V, 5V or 10V while it is off
Sets the range of that colour and overrides its button: 1V and above the widest, minus 1V and below the narrowest, and between them the middle one
Quantizes that colour's fixed voltages to semitones, and narrows the voltage its range covers
Makes that colour's step knobs set a fixed voltage within the range chosen for that colour
Makes that colour a fresh random draw on each step, the step knob setting the span it covers, from minus 5V fully anticlockwise to 5V fully clockwise
Makes that colour take the signal at its external input, scaled by the step knob of the step being played
Sets how that colour's step knobs treat its external input: as an attenuverter from minus 100% to 100%, or as a gain from 0 to 200%
The signal that colour plays while its external source is chosen, scaled by the step knob of the step being played
Switches between playing one of the two values at each step and always playing the blue value with the yellow one added on the steps that came out yellow
A trigger here switches between playing one of the two values at each step and adding the two together
Flips the step now playing to the other colour
A trigger here flips the step now playing to the other colour
Each press shortens the sequence by one step, from eight down to one and then back to eight
Sets the number of steps and overrides the length button, eight steps at 0V falling to one step at 10V
A rising edge here advances the sequence by one step, while the clock sources button takes this input
A rising edge here advances the sequence by a weighted random 1 to 8 steps, while the clock sources button takes this input
Steps through taking both clock inputs, the certain clock alone, and the uncertain clock alone
Starts and stops the sequence
A trigger here starts and stops the sequence
Returns the sequence to its first step
A rising edge here returns the sequence to its first step
Advances the sequence by one step for each press, whether or not it is running
Returns the sequence to its first step whenever run is switched on
The value of the step now playing, blue or yellow according to that step's chance, or the two added together in the adding macrostate mode
Note — the sequence does not advance until a clock arrives; the module comes up running, and the run button stops and starts it
Entropia.notes: Inputs 11 and 12 are named 'Unused blue' and 'Unused yellow' in the code and have no widget on the panel, so they cannot be clicked and are left untagged. The two external signal inputs take audio or CV depending on the CV/audio button, so they are given no family.

lines: A ring modulation oscillator and synth voice: the M sine multiplied by the square of the C sine
Sets the pitch of that oscillator across plus or minus 3 octaves, added to the voltage at the 1V/oct input
Steps that oscillator's pitch knob through a free sweep, semitones, fifths and octaves, and a 10V drop that takes it down to LFO range
Steps what that oscillator's own frequency input does: nothing, add its voltage to the pitch knob, or scale the pitch knob by that voltage taken as 0V to 10V
The frequency CV for that oscillator, added to its pitch knob or scaling it according to that oscillator's mod type button, and read by neither while that button is off
Chooses what the M pitch does to C: nothing, add the M pitch offset to C's, or subtract it from C's
Sets how much of that oscillator's own output is fed back into its own frequency, from none to full
Raises that oscillator's feedback by a tenth of full per volt; with momentum crossing on, a positive voltage here raises this oscillator's feedback and a negative one raises the other oscillator's
Sends a negative voltage at either momentum input to the other oscillator's feedback instead of its own, and doubles what both momentum inputs add
Scales the output from silence at 0V to full at 10V, slewed to avoid clicks; with nothing patched here the output stays at full
Sets the pitch of both oscillators at one volt per octave, and the number of channels here sets the polyphony
The M sine multiplied by the square of the C sine, scaled by the multiply input
A two-oscillator complex voice combining cross modulation, self modulation and ring modulation, with a ring output and one output per oscillator
Sets the pitch of that oscillator across plus or minus 3 octaves, added to the 1V/oct input and to the centre pitch knob
Steps that oscillator's pitch knob through a free sweep, fifths and octaves, and a 10V drop that takes it down to LFO range
Shifts the pitch of both oscillators together across plus or minus 3 octaves
Adds to the pitch of that oscillator at one volt per octave
Sets the pitch of both oscillators at one volt per octave, and the number of channels here sets the polyphony
Sets how much the other oscillator modulates this one's frequency, from none to full
Attenuverts the cross modulation CV before it is added to both cross modulation amounts, or to one of them when the CV mode button splits them
Modulates the cross modulation amount by a tenth of full per volt, after the centre cross modulation knob attenuverts it
Sets how much of that oscillator's own output is fed back into its own frequency, from none to full
Attenuverts the self modulation CV before it is added to both self modulation amounts, or to one of them when the CV mode button splits them
Modulates the self modulation amount by a tenth of full per volt, after the centre self modulation knob attenuverts it
Chooses, for cross modulation and again for self modulation, whether its CV moves both oscillators together, or a positive CV moves C alone and a negative CV moves M alone
A 0V to 10V signal shaped by a 2.5ms rise and the decay knob into the extra modulation envelope; with nothing patched here that envelope is fired by every change at the 1V/oct input
Sets how long the extra modulation envelope takes to fall, 2ms to 2 seconds
Lengthens the extra modulation decay, the whole 2ms to 2 seconds span across 0V to 10V, added to the decay knob
Makes the extra modulation envelope set the level of the energy output and the C output; with it off both stay at full
Steps through where the extra modulation envelope is sent: nowhere, the cross modulation CV, the self modulation CV, or both of them
Restarts the phase of both oscillators
A rising edge here restarts the phase of that oscillator
The M sine multiplied by the square of the C sine and inverted, scaled by the extra modulation envelope while the amp button is on
The M oscillator's sine on its own
The square of the C oscillator's sine, scaled by the extra modulation envelope while the amp button is on
DarkEnergy.notes: The output marked C carries the square of the C sine with the extra modulation VCA applied, not the raw C sine; the M output is the plain sine.

lines: A mixer in which every output carries a blend of the patched inputs, each weighted by how far its jack is from that output
Steps through three ways an input reaches the outputs: falling away with distance, at full level on every output, or filtered, an output below an input low-passing it and one above it high-passing it
Scales every output from silence to twice the level, applied after the mix and clamped to plus or minus 10V
A signal fed into the mix, reaching each output at a level set by its distance from this jack; the channels of a polyphonic cable here are summed
The blend of the patched inputs weighted by their distance from this jack, scaled by the gain knob
Menu — Filters — the slope used in filter mode: 6dB per octave, or 12dB per octave, which is the default
An event modifier that on each trigger may swap two signals between its outputs and add a random offset to each
Sets the chance that a trigger alters fate, never fully anticlockwise and every trigger fully clockwise
Every volt here adds a tenth to the chance that a trigger alters fate, on top of the free will knob
A rising edge here draws a new fate, deciding whether the two signals swap outputs and what random offsets are added
A signal passed to its own output, or to the other output when the draw alters fate; with the other event input empty this signal feeds both outputs
The signal from its own input, or from the other input when the draw alters fate, with that draw's random offset added
10V while the last draw altered fate, lasting as long as the incoming trigger, or until the next draw with the menu option set
Scales the random offsets added when fate is altered, none at the centre and plus or minus 5V at either end; anticlockwise the first output takes only positive offsets and the second only negative
Widens the random offsets added when fate is altered by a tenth of their span per volt, added to the choice depth knob
Note — nothing is drawn until a trigger arrives at the clock input
Note — with nothing patched to the event inputs the outputs carry the random offsets alone, which makes the module a pair of probabilistic random sources
Menu — Hold trigger out during step — holds the trigger output high until the next draw, rather than only for the length of the incoming trigger
A clock generator with two outputs that can run at different rates through a group of beats and always come back together at its end
Turns the tempo up or down between 30 and 300 BPM; the tempo comes from the sync input instead while a cable is patched there
Taps in the tempo, averaged over the last four taps; presses are ignored while a cable is in the sync input
Steps the reference tempo through plain, divided by 2, divided by 4, multiplied by 2 and multiplied by 4, a green lamp for a division and a violet one for a multiplication
Steps how the sync input is read, through a voltage carrying the tempo, 24 pulses per quarter note and 48; two quick pulses at that input also switch it to 24
Sets the tempo from outside, as a clock at 24 or 48 pulses per quarter note, or as a voltage where 0V is 120 BPM and every volt doubles it
Steps what the sync output carries, through a clock at the reference tempo, one at 24 times it, one at 48 times it, and a voltage carrying the tempo
A clock at the reference tempo or at 24 or 48 times it, or a voltage where 0V is 120 BPM and every volt doubles it
Sets the reference group at 1 to 8 beats, the span over which the twins go apart and meet again
Lengthens the reference group, the whole 1 to 8 beat span across 0V to 10V, added to the reference time knob
Sets how many beats, 1 to 8, the travelling twin fits into the span of the reference group
Lengthens the traveller's group, the whole 1 to 8 beat span across 0V to 10V, added to the traveler time knob
Requests a travel, which begins at the start of the next reference group
A trigger here requests a travel, which begins at the start of the next reference group
Sets the chance of a travel beginning at each new reference group, never fully anticlockwise and every group fully clockwise
Every volt here adds a tenth to the chance of a travel beginning at a new group, on top of the auto-travel knob
Sets which twin takes the travelling timeline, twin 1 every time fully anticlockwise, twin 2 every time fully clockwise, and a random pick between them
Every volt here adds a tenth to the chance of twin 2 being the traveller, on top of the traveler knob
The twin 1 clock, which runs the reference tempo except while twin 1 is the traveller
The twin 2 clock, which runs the reference tempo except while twin 2 is the traveller
A 1ms 10V pulse each time a reference group completes and the twins meet, or only at the end of a travel with the menu option set
Starts and stops the clocks; with a clock patched to the sync input in a pulses per quarter note reading it can only stop them
A trigger here starts and stops the clocks, or holds them running for as long as it is high with the menu option set
A 1ms 10V pulse when the clocks start and another when they stop
Returns the clocks to the start of a reference group
A rising edge here returns the clocks to the start of a reference group
A 1ms 10V pulse whenever the module is reset, and on starting or stopping with the matching menu option set
Note — the clocks come up running as soon as the module is added, and the run button stops and starts them
Menu — On Start — what starting the clocks also does, either, both or neither of Do internal reset and Send reset pulse
Menu — On Stop — what stopping the clocks also does, either, both or neither of Do internal reset and Send reset pulse
Menu — Outputs high on reset when not running — holds the clock outputs at 10V while the module is reset and stopped, in place of 0V
Menu — Run CV input is gate (instead of trigger) — makes the run input follow the level of a gate rather than toggling on each rising edge
Menu — Meet only at end of travel — limits the meet output to the groups that end a travel
A blank panel printing the Geodesics name, its version and its authors, with no controls
Menu — Panel Theme — Use Rack global theme follows Rack's own light and dark setting, while White light edition and Dark matter edition pick one outright
A blank panel carrying the Geodesics logo, with a hidden clock and a five-note melody
Sets the rate of the hidden clock that steps the melody, 15 to 960 BPM with 120 BPM at the default
Steps through a five-note melody, one note per beat of the hidden clock, as pitches at one volt per octave
Menu — Panel Theme — Use Rack global theme follows Rack's own light and dark setting, while White light edition and Dark matter edition pick one outright
